branch: cmdTakesArg: any argumentHint inserts '/name ' and waits; only a hint-less command runs on click
provenance: Roster entry shapes ({name, description, argumentHint, aliases?}, no type field; custom entries marked only by a ' (project)'/' (user)' description suffix) are fixture 46's, measured 2026-08-15 on CLI 2.1.228. The argumentHint VALUES here were MEASURED OFF THE WIRE on 2026-08-17: a bare `initialize` control request to CLI 2.1.233 (the panel's own flags, no user turn) returns 51 entries whose keys are exactly {name, description, argumentHint, aliases?} — confirming again there is no type field, and no `immediate` flag either, though the binary carries one internally. Measured hints used here: /compact '<optional custom summarization instructions>', /context '[init | load | save | <note to record>]' (this repo's skill, shadowing the built-in whose hint is '[all]'), /loop '[interval] [prompt]', /config 'key=value' (the bracket-less shape). An earlier `strings` pass had attributed '[<condition> | clear]' to /goal; the wire sends /goal an EMPTY hint — the binary holds two records for it and only one reaches the roster. The project skill's own hint '[init | load | save | <note to record>]' is this repo's .claude/skills/context/SKILL.md frontmatter, which shadows the built-in /context in the roster. __commands is a PLUGIN-INTERNAL frame (ChatPanel's initialize relay), so assertions stay on what the renderer must do with the shape it is handed. The click steps swap window.__bridge for a recorder inside a try/finally — no turn ever reaches the CLI, and a throw cannot leave the panel mute. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN 2026-08-17 against commit 4e351f4's chat.html (the last cmdNeedsArg build — pinned, not a relative ref): all 7 DISCRIMINATING assertions failed and all 12 GUARDs passed — the assertions marked DISCRIMINATING fail, the GUARDs stay green. The hint-shape guards go through the RENDERED data-takesarg attribute rather than calling cmdTakesArg directly: on the pre-fix build the function does not exist, and a ReferenceError aborts the whole harness run before the control can report anything (hit 2026-08-16). Step 3 resets busy/log before its click on purpose: without it the PRE-fix build arrives with busy=true from step 2's send, submit() queues the turn instead of sending it, and two guards fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the rule under test (fixture 44's masking trap, found by running this control 2026-08-16).
